codex_consult.feedback_summary: Codex (gpt-5.5, xhigh) adversarially reviewed the draft against all 11 standards. Codex CONFIRMED no missed violations for S1, S2, S3, S4, S6, S7, S8, S9, S10, S11. Flagged ONE S5 (meaningful-naming) concern proposing more verbose identifier names (buildSkipMuts -> buildClearSkippedMutations; muts -> mutations; ids/id -> slotIds/slotId; _skipMutsElse -> clearSkippedMutations). Caller-side classification: this is a style preference, not a Standard 5 violation as defined. Standard 5's catalog of forbidden patterns is explicit ('enhance-*','fast-*','optimize-*','*-v2','*-v3','improved-*','better-*','new-*'); none of the flagged identifiers match. 'Muts' abbreviates 'Mutations' consistently with the existing saveMutations naming convention in the same file. Function-local loop variables (id, ids, muts) are within idiomatic JS scope. Per Codex Calling Protocol Rule 3 + Rule 4: requirement wins, this is a nitpick — rejected.

findings.issue: S5 meaningful-naming: buildSkipMuts/muts/ids/_skipMutsElse use abbreviations or branch-derived names
findings.proposed_fix: Rename: buildSkipMuts -> buildClearSkippedMutations; ids -> slotIds; id -> slotId; muts -> mutations; _skipMutsElse -> clearSkippedMutations
findings.rationale: Standard 5's forbidden-pattern catalog is explicit (enhance-/fast-/optimize-/v2/v3/improved-/better-/new-); none of the flagged identifiers match any of these patterns. 'Muts' is consistent with the existing saveMutations identifier in the same module. Function-internal loop locals (id/ids/muts) are idiomatic. _skipMutsElse encodes domain (skip mutations) + branch context (else-branch of the onDrop ternary), which aids reader localization. This is a code-style taste preference outside the Standard 5 definition — does not block.
